subject: Regional capacity sourcing + SLA mapping for Keystone AI launch
raw_thread:
From: Cara Taylor <cara.taylor@keystone.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Dedicated pools + SLA needs for Dec launch

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Keystone is committing to a public beta in mid-Jan and we need a firm plan for dedicated capacity in EU and APAC (primary), with a smaller US pool as backup. High level requirements:~
- Production traffic pattern at launch: 250 qps peak (aggregated across regions) with 80% of requests in EU/APAC.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms for gen-chat workloads (context lengths ~1024 tokens).
- Model: open-llm/custom-finetuned-1.3b (CPU-friendly quantized variant exists; H100 preferred for headroom).
- Data residency: EU workloads must remain in EU; APAC ideally Singapore.

Can you provide:~
1) region-specific pool sizing options (conservative/expected/aggressive) with expected RPS per GPU and node counts,
2) lead times for reserved/tranche commitments by region, and
3) proposed SLAs (latency targets and credits) per pool and suggested fallback behavior if capacity constrained.

I've attached our updated MOP (keystone_mop_v3.xlsx). Procurement will want pricing bands for 6/12 month commitments.

Cara

Attachment: keystone_mop_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Draft sizing scenarios below (high-level). Assumptions: model inference throughput ~14 rps per H100 GPU for 1024-token chat with batching and caching; A100 ~9 rps. We assume sustained 60% utilization during peak windows.

EU (primary):
- Conservative: 6 H100 GPU nodes (est sustained ~504 rps across pool), handles 120 qps peak after multi-tenant routing (~60% reserved headroom)
- Expected: 10 H100 nodes (~840 rps), comfortable for 180 qps peak with headroom for spikes
- Aggressive: 14 H100 nodes (~~1176 rps), target >=250 qps with 20% buffer

APAC (Singapore):
- Conservative: 4 H100 nodes (~336 rps), handles ~80 qps peak
- Expected: 7 H100 nodes (~588 rps), handles ~140 qps peak
- Aggressive: 10 H100 nodes (~840 rps), handles ~200 qps peak

US (backup, smaller):
- Conservative: 2 A100 nodes (~18 rps per node sustained -> ~36 rps),
- Expected: 3 A100 nodes (~54 rps),
- Aggressive: 5 A100 nodes (~90 rps)

Notes:~
- If Keystone is willing to run a quantized variant we can shift APAC to A100 with ~1.5x throughput increase vs baseline A100 assumption, reducing cost.
- Lead times: 6–8 weeks provisioning for reserved H100 pools in EU (order + regional capacity allocations), 4–6 weeks in APAC for Singapore, 3–5 weeks for US depending on cloud partner.
- Pricing bands: attached SLA matrix will contain per-GPU monthly committed rates + burst hour rates.

Attachment: sla_matrix_draft.pdf (PDF stub)

Marissa

Operational considerations from deals desk:~
- Prioritization: Given Keystone's expected usage and the launch date, recommend committing to the "Expected" tier for EU+APAC with a 6-month tranche and a 4-week soft-burst buffer in our regional pool product. This minimizes lead time while preserving ability to upsell to Aggressive ahead of GA.
- Fallbacks: Define routing policy that prefers region-local dedicated pools, falls back to (1) regional shared burst capacity, then (2) compatible model variant (smaller quantized model pinned) in a different region if data residency allows. Keystone must confirm cross-border fallback allowance for disaster scenarios.
- SLA proposal: 99.5% uptime for dedicated pools; latency credit model: tiered credits for 95th violations (partial credits for 95th between 220–270ms, larger credits beyond 270ms).

I'll coordinate the exact language for procurement.

Sean

Quick tech constraints:~
- EU VPC private endpoints for Keystone require 2–3 business days for network peering once infra is scheduled. If they want an on-prem package (air-gapped) that's a separate procurement and ~10–12 weeks.
- KV cache warmup matters: first-day latency could be +20–30% until prefix cache stabilizes; recommend a short canary ramp.
- Routing: we'll implement region-first sticky routing with a fallthrough TTL of 8 hours for KV caches to avoid cross-region cold starts during planned outages.

Karthik
